title: Gongguan Walk: NTU, Water Park and Treasure Hill
excerpt: A full-day walk from Technology Building MRT across the NTU campus, through Taipei Water Park and its old pumping station to Treasure Hill Art Village, finishing at Gongguan Night Market.
content:
This is the longest self-guided walk on this site, and a proper day out. It begins on the leafy campus of National Taiwan University (NTU), one of the nicest corners of central Taipei, stops in Gongguan for lunch, then climbs through Taipei Water Park and its century-old pumping station to Treasure Hill, a hillside settlement turned artists' village with views back over the city. You finish in Gongguan as the night market is getting busy. The numbered route covers about 5.8km, and with breakfast, lunch, a museum or two and the night market it takes 8 to 10 hours, so wear your walking boots!

Choose your day with care. Taipei Water Park and Treasure Hill both close on Mondays, and for most of the year the Water Park sells its last tickets at 16:00, which sets the pace for the afternoon. The best time to go section has the details. For more on the neighbourhood itself, see the Gongguan guide.

The Route

If you'd rather wake up near the start, the Daan hotels guide lists the nearest MRT station for each of its picks, and Technology Building, where this route begins, is one of them.

Step-By-Step

  • 1 Take the brown line to Technology Building station
    • Have breakfast before you set off. Yong He Soy Milk King, about 400m north up Fuxing South Road, is the choice for a traditional Taiwanese breakfast of soy milk, fried dough sticks and egg pancakes
    • For a western-style breakfast or brunch, the original branch of The Diner is a similar distance west, on Ruian Street
    • Yong He used to be famous for staying open through the night, but a June 2026 report gives its hours as 05:00–14:00, closed on Mondays. It is a breakfast stop either way
  • 2 Walk south down Fuxing South Road, turn right along Xinhai Road and enter the NTU campus at Drunken Moon Lake
    • The campus is open to the public and you can wander it at your own pace. The university's visitor centre runs guided tours, but only for booked groups such as school parties and official visitors
    • The lake sits on the northern edge of the campus, beside the sports grounds, and makes a peaceful first stop
  • 3 Carry on through the campus. It covers about 110 hectares, so you are free to roam as you please
    • Stop 3 is the heart of the old campus, with the main university buildings and the Fu Bell
    • The bell stands on Royal Palm Boulevard, which runs for more than 600m from the main gate up to the Main Library, and it is struck 21 times to mark the end of classes, after Fu Ssu-nien's remark that a day has 21 hours and the last three are for thinking
    • There are a few cafés dotted around the campus if you need a drink break
  • 4 Head down the boulevard towards the main gate and Fu Yuan, the memorial garden where Fu Ssu-nien's tomb stands inside a Greek-style colonnade
    • Several of the campus museums are on the way to stop 4, close to the main gate
    • [optional] The Museum of Anthropology opens 10:00–16:00 on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, and 09:00–17:00 on Saturday. It is closed on Tuesdays, Sundays and national holidays
    • [optional] The Gallery of NTU History is in the old library building next door. Check its hours before going, as they were not published when this walk was updated
    • [optional] The NTU Herbarium exhibition room opens from 10:00 to noon and again from 13:00 to 16:00, and is closed on Tuesdays and public holidays
  • 5 Leave the campus by the main gate and cross Roosevelt Road into Gongguan
    • The lanes just across the road are packed with restaurants and food stalls, so this is the place for lunch. I've marked a few on the map above, and they are described under Where to Eat
    • Gongguan MRT exit 3 is right outside the gate if you need to cut the day short
  • 6 Walk south-west to the Siyuan Street entrance of Taipei Water Park and visit the Drinking Water Museum, which has been exquisitely preserved
    • The museum is the pumping station of the Japanese-era Taipei waterworks, completed in 1908 and taken out of service in 1977. It was declared a historic site in 1993 and later restored to its original look
    • Entry to the park, museum included, is NT$50 from September to June and NT$80 in July and August, with half-price tickets for children and students. Visitors aged 65 and over and children under 6 go free
    • Hours are 09:00–17:00 from September to June (last tickets 16:00) and 09:00–18:00 in July and August (last tickets 17:00). It is closed on Mondays, unless the Monday falls in a run of public holidays
    • Scheduled tours of the museum, about 30 minutes long, set off from the square in front at 10:00 and 14:00, Tuesday to Sunday
  • 7 Explore the Water Park paths and trails behind the museum
    • The trail passes the old backwash sand pool, a viewing platform beside the surge tower and an area of sculptures made from water pipes, then climbs to the Guanyinshan Reservoir, where you'll get some nice views
    • [optional] The reservoir's interior, nicknamed the Underground Water Palace, can only be seen on a guided tour, at 14:30 on Thursdays and Saturdays, lasting about 50 minutes. Places are limited to 30, and numbered tickets are handed out at the ticket office on the day, so collect one when you arrive. The tour is cancelled in thunderstorms
    • Near the top, a path leads to a one-way turnstile that lets you out into Treasure Hill. You can't come back through it, so see everything you want in the Water Park first, and go through before the park closes
  • 8 Wander down through Treasure Hill Art Village, visit some of the exhibitions or even watch some artists at work
    • Coming in from the Water Park puts you near the top, so most of the steps are downhill from here
    • The lanes and outdoor spaces are open Tuesday to Sunday, 11:00–22:00, and the indoor galleries and studios 11:00–18:00. The whole village is closed on Mondays
    • It is free to walk around, though a few exhibitions charge. The 2026 Winter Open Studios runs until 29 November
    • There are also some nice cafés in the village
  • 9 Walk back into Gongguan along Tingzhou Road to Gongguan Night Market
    • The market runs every day from 15:00 to 23:45, according to Taipei Travel, so it will be open by now, though some stalls only start in the early evening
    • There are a couple of Michelin-recommended stands here. Hsiung Chi Scallion Pancake, by the Lane 108 entrance, is on the 2026 Bib Gourmand list
    • Don't miss the delicious gua bao at Lan Jia Traditional Taiwanese Snack, which was given a Bib Gourmand in 2019, although it does not appear on the 2026 list

Where to Eat

  • Yong He Soy Milk King, 102 Fuxing South Road Section 2, for a cheap Taiwanese breakfast near the start. Its hours are now reported as 05:00–14:00, closed Mondays
  • The Diner, 145 Ruian Street, serves western breakfasts all day
  • Lan Jia, in Alley 8, Lane 316, Roosevelt Road Section 3, works just as well for lunch as for dinner. A 2025 report gives its hours as 11:00–22:00, closed on Mondays
  • YU POKÉ, in Alley 12, Lane 24, Roosevelt Road Section 4, makes build-your-own poke bowls, a fresher option among all the fried snacks
  • Madame Jill's Vietnamese Cuisine (翠薪越南餐廳), at 11 Lane 24, Roosevelt Road Section 4, has been serving pho and spring rolls near NTU since the mid-1970s. It opens for lunch and dinner, with a break in the afternoon
  • El Sabroso, at 107-1 Tingzhou Road Section 3, is a small Mexican kitchen known for its burritos and quesadillas, with tacos on Tuesdays
  • The cafés in Treasure Hill are handy for a break between stops 7 and 9

Best Time to Go

  • Avoid Mondays. Taipei Water Park and Treasure Hill are both closed, which removes the best part of the afternoon
  • Thursday or Saturday is best, because those are the days of the reservoir tour, and the Museum of Anthropology is open on both
  • Between September and June, aim to reach the Water Park by about 14:00. The last tickets are sold at 16:00 and the park closes at 17:00, and you need to be through the turnstile to Treasure Hill before then
  • Treasure Hill's indoor spaces close at 18:00, so you reach Gongguan Night Market around dusk
  • July and August give you an extra hour in the Water Park, but the heat makes a long day on foot hard work, so take plenty of water
  • On typhoon days, when the city shuts its venues, both the Water Park and Treasure Hill close too. Treasure Hill shut for one on 23 and 24 October 2026

Getting There and Back

Start: Technology Building station on the brown (Wenhu) line, two stops south of Zhongxiao Fuxing.

Finish: Gongguan station on the green line, a few minutes' walk from the night market. Exit 1 is the closest to the market and to Treasure Hill, exit 3 is beside the NTU main gate, and exit 4 is the one for the Water Park. Gongguan is three stops south of Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall. The MRT guide covers fares and the rest of the network.

For a shorter day, start at Gongguan exit 3 and walk into the campus through the main gate, which cuts out the walk from Technology Building and Drunken Moon Lake. The route does not work in reverse, because the turnstile between the Water Park and Treasure Hill only lets people out.

Common Questions

How long is the Gongguan walk?

The numbered route is about 5.8km, but the walking is spread across a whole day. With meals, the museum and the night market, plan on 8 to 10 hours. Starting at Gongguan instead of Technology Building saves around half an hour.

Can anyone walk around National Taiwan University?

Yes. The campus is open to the public and nobody needs to book to walk around it. The guided tours run by the NTU Visitor Center are only for booked groups, so most visitors explore on their own.

How much does Taipei Water Park cost?

NT$50 from September to June and NT$80 in July and August, with concession tickets at half price. The ticket covers the Drinking Water Museum and the trails.

Can you get to Treasure Hill from the Water Park?

Yes. A path near the reservoir leads to a one-way turnstile into Treasure Hill. You can't come back the same way, and you have to go through before the Water Park closes at 17:00 (18:00 in July and August).

Which day should I avoid?

Monday, when Taipei Water Park and Treasure Hill are both closed. Tuesday is also weaker, as the Museum of Anthropology and the NTU Herbarium are closed that day.

Carry On Walking

Next door to the north, the Daan walking route crosses Daan Forest Park, about 15 minutes on foot north-west of Technology Building, then carries on to Yongkang Street. The Zhongzheng walking route starts at Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall, three stops north of Gongguan on the green line. Every walk is listed under Routes.
